haiku-low.q1: It acknowledges accepted events with 202, returned only after the log confirms the write. The body lists rejected events by index and event_id. The rest of the batch is kept.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, with backoff starting at 1 s and capped at 5 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy in log order, the winner, goes to events_clean. Later copies are duplicates and are not written there.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday. Its day, partition and replay use received_at, the server's UTC time, not the client timestamp.
haiku-low.q5: In a key-value store, one key per event_id, valued with the winner's log position. A 9-day TTL removes old entries.
haiku-low.q6: Deduplication stops and its offset does not advance. Events wait in the log, and the freshness alert fires. The document does not say whether clients are affected.
haiku-low.q7: The dedup offset is saved only after the warehouse confirms the batch. A crash before that causes a re-read and double write, and the seal removes the copies. Nothing is lost.
haiku-low.q8: Replay reads the raw archive and manifest, never the live log. Rebuilt rows go to a staging table, then atomically replace partition D of events_clean.
haiku-low.q9: It keeps only manifest rows marked winner, without re-deciding dedup. It finds each winner's raw copy by log position, so earlier-day winners are included and retry copies are never used.
haiku-low.q10: events_clean is left unchanged, the staging rows are discarded, and the ledger records the failure. The operator can run the replay again.
haiku-low.q11: Only sealed days still in the raw archive and manifest, which are kept 90 days. Replay refuses any day that is not sealed.
haiku-low.q12: Product has not decided. The plan offers dropping suspected bot events or keeping them with a flag column, and does not choose.

sonnet.q1: It returns 202 only after the log confirms the durable write of the accepted events. Malformed events are rejected individually (missing event_id/device_id, or over 32 KB); the rest of the batch is kept. The 202 body lists rejected events by index and event_id.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, with backoff starting at 1 s and capping at 5 minutes. (Mobile SDK buffers on device for up to 7 days.)
sonnet.q3: The first copy in log order (the winner) goes to events_clean; later copies are duplicates and are not written there (they stay in the archive and manifest).
sonnet.q4: Day Tuesday (UTC day of received_at, 00:10 Tuesday). Client time is never used for day, partition or replay.
sonnet.q5: In the key-value store: one key per event_id whose value is the winner's log position, set only if absent. Entries expire via a 9-day TTL. (Day records live there too, with no TTL.)
sonnet.q6: Clients are not described as affected beyond the collector/log path. Deduplication stops and does not advance its offset; events wait in the log (14-day retention) and the freshness alert fires.
sonnet.q7: Not lost: the dedup offset is saved only after the warehouse confirms the batch, so the batch is re-read on restart. Double-counting: the key-value store still marks each as winner (same position), so they are re-processed as winners, but the batch may be written twice to events_clean; the design does not prevent this live. The seal removes the extra copies later, and until then dashboards can see them.
sonnet.q8: Input is the raw archive and the manifest (winner rows for day D), not the live log. Rebuilt rows are written to the staging table, which dashboards never read, then swapped into partition D.
sonnet.q9: It reads the manifest's decisions: keeps only rows marked winner for day D (no dedup re-run), and fetches each winner's raw copy by its log position (partition and offset). A retry copy has a different position so is never used. Manifest records the decision at first dedup, so earlier-day first copies are handled by the recorded decision.
sonnet.q10: events_clean is unchanged (staging rows are discarded; if the swap fails, the old day stays). The ledger records the failure. The operator can run the replay again.
sonnet.q11: Only sealed days, and only those still in the raw archive and manifest (90-day retention), with target enrichment versions whose geo-IP and UA files are stored.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Product has not decided: either drop suspected bots or keep them with a flag column; the plan does not choose.
